summary.summary:
Migrated rdflib-sqlalchemy from SQLAlchemy 1.4 to 2.0 APIs. Code changes:
- rdflib_sqlalchemy/sql.py: select([...], where) list/positional forms replaced with select(*cols).where(...) via a new apply_where() helper (None clause = no restriction, avoiding WHERE NULL); from_obj= replaced with select_from(); union/union_all(..., order_by=...) replaced with .order_by(...) on the compound select; COUNT subquery wrapped with explicit .subquery(); query_analysis raw string wrapped in text().
- rdflib_sqlalchemy/store.py: select([col]) -> select(col) in prefix()/namespace(); namespaces() uses select(table).distinct(); all table.delete(clause) calls (remove, _remove_context) rewritten as delete(table) with apply_where().
- rdflib_sqlalchemy/statistics.py: session.query(...) replaced with session.execute(select(...).group_by(...)).
Dependency pins in setup.py: SQLAlchemy>=2.0,<3.0 (was >=1.1.4,<2.0.0); alembic floor raised to >=1.12.0 (was >=0.8.8; alembic is declared but not imported, and old releases don't support SQLAlchemy 2.0). Test result: 44 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped (skips are pre-existing and unchanged). Not verified here: the exact alembic version that first supports SQLAlchemy 2.0 (1.12.0 is my best estimate); the postgres-specific OnConflictDoNothing hack in _add_ignore_on_conflict still uses a private attribute and was not exercised by the suite (postgres tests are skipped in this environment).
